title: Shadow traffic bisect field notebook
content:
Purpose and context
---
Notes from experimenting with shadow traffic to reproduce a 95th-99th percentile latency regression seen in production canaries (INF-4823). Goal: create a repeatable sampling + bisect workflow that surfaces kernel/host bottlenecks while preserving production safety. This is a working notebook — rough, lots of TODOs.

Top-level summary (quick)
- Regression signal: sudden bump in p95/p99 for short(<64) text completions on the n1-cpu-4 baseline pool, first seen in canary cluster 3 on 2025-02-10.
- Canary vs baseline divergence shows ~30–60ms delta at p95 and a 160ms tail at p99 for specific prompts.
- Hypotheses prioritized: 1) batching changes (adaptive batch thresholds), 2) KV cache eviction pattern (prefix-churn for sampled traffic), 3) host-side pre/post-processing (tokenizer, safety checks).

Shadow traffic plan (why shadow)
- Use shadowed replica of baseline model group to run sampled production requests (no user-facing latency impact). Capture full traces, sysmetrics, and GPU traces concurrently.
- Advantages: real traffic distributions; easy to toggle sample rate; can A/B routing rules; safer than canary for high-volume bisects.
- Current sample rate: 2% across critical routes (chat.complete, text.generate). Duration for this run: 48 hours to capture diurnal variance.

Data to capture (per-request)
- request_id, route, model, model_version, seq_len_input, seq_len_output_est, batch_id, batch_size, batch_wait_ms
- KV_cache_hit (bool), kv_cache_size_at_request, kv_cache_evictions_during_request
- GPU: SM_util_pct, memory_used_mb, GPU_scheduling_wait_ms
- Host: cpu_user_ms, cpu_system_ms, preproc_ms, postproc_ms, ssl_handshake_ms, time_to_first_token_ms
- Traces: whether full callchain trace sampled (trace_id), and a link to perf artifacts (s3 path)

Prometheus / Grafana queries to reproduce signals
- p95 latency by route: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route=~"chat.*|text.*"}[5m])) by (le, route))
- batch size distribution: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum(rate(batch_size_bucket[5m])) by (le, pool))
- kv cache hit-rate: sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total[5m])) by (pool)
- gpu queuing wait: sum(rate(gpu_queue_wait_seconds_sum[5m])) / sum(rate(gpu_queue_wait_seconds_count[5m])) by (pool)

Sampling and selection heuristics (how we pick which requests to inspect)
- Focus on short prompts (input tokens <= 48) where delta is largest. Also sample ends of sessions (last turn) since cache behavior differs.
- Select top-100 failing trace examples by p99 delta, then expand to 1k random examples for statistical checks.
- Ensure we include both warm and cold KV-cache contexts. Mark requests with KV_cache_hit=false as high interest.

Bisect workflow (high-level)
1) Reproduce: run shadow experiment and confirm p95/p99 divergence on the replicated traffic.
2) Narrow by route and token-length slice. Example: chat.complete with input<=24 tokens.
3) Binary search over code/infra deltas: test last-good commit date vs first-bad commit (use snapshots). For each candidate commit, roll a small dedicated pool with that binary and replay a sample subset of recorded requests.
4) If commit bisection inconclusive: bisect config layers (batcher thresholds, autoscale policies, kernel flags, quantization toggles).
5) If still inconclusive: enable fine-grained profiling (GPU Nsight traces, kernel-level logs) on a small sample of requests.

Sample commands / snippets (replay + profiling)
- Start isolated pool with pinned binary: ./deploy/poolctl create --pool test-bisect-$(commit) --image serving-runtime:commit-abcdef --gpus 2 --labels bisect=true
- Replay requests (sanitized) into pool at realistic qps: python tools/replay.py --input s3://perf-artifacts/shadow-samples/2025-02-12.ndjson --target http://test-bisect-commit:8080 --concurrency 32 --capture-traces
- Collect GPU trace (NVIDIA Nsight): nsys profile --output /tmp/nsys.$(id).qdrep --delay 5 --trace=nvtx,cuda -- python tools/replay.py ...
- Collect host perf: sudo perf record -g -o /tmp/perf.$(id).data -- python -m replay.loader ...

Evidence matrix (notes from first 24h run)
- Observed: batch_size median fell from 6 -> 3 for short prompts after the adaptive batch change (candidate config change). Low batch sizes correlate strongly with p95 increase.
- KV cache: hit-rate dropped from 82% -> 64% for the sampled route; high eviction spikes aligned with certain user IDs (pattern suggests prefix variance).
- Host-side: preproc_ms increased ~15ms median during the noisy window — traced to a new sanitizer check added in PR #1123 (linked).
- GPU: SM_util unchanged; memory used stable; GPU queue wait increased slightly for specific hosts (suspect kernel launch overhead under small batches).

Preliminary conclusions
- Primary contributor: reduced effective batching for small prompts — when batch size drops, kernel launch overhead and per-request postproc dominate p95.
- Secondary: KV cache churn amplifies the effect for some user slices because more tokens are re-computed instead of cached (cold starts increase latency variance).
- Tertiary: the sanitizer PR added ~10–20ms in preproc for some inputs; contributes to median but not the entire tail.

Immediate mitigations (fast follow)
- Temporarily increase min_batch_size for short routes to restore batching behavior (config flip): rollout to test pool and shadow-run 6h. Owner: Priya Nair, priority: high.
- Roll back sanitizer check in PR #1123 behind feature flag, or gate on input size. Owner: Jonah Rivera, priority: medium.
- Increase KV cache capacity for the pool and monitor eviction rate. Owner: Marta Delgado, priority: medium.

Open questions / TODOs
- Is the adaptive batch threshold tuning working as intended for low-latency SLAs? Can we switch to a latency-first threshold for short routes? (Action: compare policy configs INF-CONF-71)
- Why are certain user ID prefixes showing higher eviction rates? Correlate with prompt templates and session length. (Action: add tag extraction to shadow capture)
- Need per-kernel launch timing: are we seeing driver-side stalls or true kernel overhead? (Action: capture CU-level timings with CUPTI)

Follow-ups and action log
- 2025-02-15: ran 48h shadow capture (sample rate 2%). Data in s3://perf-artifacts/shadow/2025-02-15-48h/ (sanitized). Owner: Marta Delgado.
- 2025-02-16: validated that increasing min_batch_size to 4 (test pool) reduces p95 by ~18ms in replay. Owner: Priya Nair.
- 2025-02-18: rolled sanitizer behind flag in test; retest pending. Owner: Jonah Rivera.

Appendix: quick checklist for a new investigator
- Step 0: read INF-4823 and this notebook.
- Step 1: enable shadow sample pipeline (2%) and confirm data retention to S3.
- Step 2: run the Prom queries above to reproduce divergence on Grafana. Save dashboard snapshot.
- Step 3: pick 100 top-variance trace ids -> run targeted replay with nsys and perf attached.
- Step 4: try min_batch_size bump to 4 on a small test pool and replay; compare p95/p99.
- Step 5: if kernel-level suspicion remains, escalate to applied-ml for kernel/profile analysis.

Notes to self: keep this notebook minimal and link more formal root-cause writeups to Confluence when we have final RCA. Also: coordinate with SRE for any rolling config flips to avoid knock-on capacity issues.
